fact: Telecel Money mobile money is in service in the Central African Republic, with many ENERCA subscribers already paying electricity bills through it before the official launch on 4 August 2026, according to Telecel and ENERCA.

The CEMAC QR Code standard, launched 29 July 2026 across six states including the Central African Republic, lets a client with a bank account, mobile money wallet or microfinance account pay by scan whatever their institution.
GIMACPAY, the CEMAC card-mobile-transfer ecosystem in service since 2021, processed over sixteen million mobile transactions in 2025.
GIMAC said that in the first half of 2026 payment institutions and mobile money operators, including those of the Central African Republic, dominate GIMACPAY transaction volumes.
GIMACPAY links 56 banks, 26 microfinance institutions, 16 payment institutions and mobile money operators and 52 aggregators across the CEMAC, which processed 20.3 million transactions in 2025.
Orange mobile money transfer and mobile payment services operate in Batangafo, but have been down for nearly a month, per local testimony reported by Corbeau News.
Orange Centrafrique provides its Orange Money mobile payment infrastructure, described as widely used across the country, to pay the DPI import fee, per the finance ministry's chief of staff.
AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY, live since July 2020, carries P2P and merchant payments to and from 11 mobile money operators across the six CEMAC states including the Central African Republic.
AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY gives all-to-all interoperability between banks, microfinance institutions and mobile money operators in the six CEMAC states including the Central African Republic.
AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY also provides domestic instant payment functionality connecting banks and mobile money wallets in each CEMAC state, including the Central African Republic.
The article reports that Orange RCA runs an Orange Money mobile money service in the Central African Republic and raised its transaction fees, which the minister ordered suspended (April 2024).

Ecomatin reports that mobile money transactions in the Central African Republic have been taxed at 1% under the 2024 finance law since 1 January 2024, and that the country had about 150,000 mobile money accounts, 65,000 active monthly, at end August 2021.
